facts.windowsInterpretation: User-mode fail-fast exception status; fail-fast subcode is unavailable.

supportingEvidence: Matching CHILD_EXITED row in engine-launch-lifecycle.jsonl includes PID 8524, launcher PID 44084, exitCode -1073740791, and exitedAt.
Matching instance JSONL ends 1.240 seconds before the launcher-observed exit.
First failed HTTP observation occurs 21m47.699s after process exit.
No normal SHUTDOWN_REQUESTED, ENGINE_FATAL_HANDLER, UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION_MONITOR, or PROCESS_EXIT row exists for PID 8524 in the captured process lifecycle file.

separateCategories.PROCESS_EXIT_NORMAL_OR_EXTERNAL: CONTRADICTED as the primary classification; no graceful shutdown record and a fail-fast exit status are present. An unobserved external termination mechanism cannot be absolutely excluded without an OS trace or dump.
separateCategories.PROCESS_ALIVE_HTTP_UNAVAILABLE: CONTRADICTED for the time of failure because the child has a matching process exit receipt; HTTP was not tested at the exact exit instant.
separateCategories.RESOURCE_PRESSURE_OR_NATIVE_FAILURE: Native fail-fast termination is PROVEN as the exit class. Four Windows System Event ID 2004 records provide STRONG_EVIDENCE of system low-virtual-memory pressure 4m50s before exit; PID 8524 is not named among the top three processes. Whether that pressure caused or contributed to this process exit remains UNKNOWN without PID-specific counters or a dump.
separateCategories.MULTIPLE_OR_UNKNOWN_TRIGGER: UNKNOWN for the initiating code path, native module, fast-fail subcode, and instruction stack.
